solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lords and ladies give up preaching?

parts.note: to jack in is British slang for quitting or abandoning something
the pulpit stands for preaching and the clergy's work as a whole

explanation.surface: A question about whether aristocrats should abandon going to church to hear sermons.
explanation.walkthrough: Lords and ladies is not the peerage but a wild arum plant; the question mark flags the whimsical reading of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords and ladies is a common British name for the wild arum, a plant also called jack-in-the-pulpit.

clue.text: How something funny appears initially just in the eye

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word just

parts.note: the word just supplies its own first letter
ocular means relating to or seen by the eye

explanation.surface: A musing that humour lies, to begin with, purely in the eye of the beholder.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark meant humorously is described as jocular, meaning joking or playful in manner.

clue.text: Run out of gear with nothing in shed

indicators.note: in tells us the zero for nothing is placed inside the word meaning shed

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin
O is the round zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Instructions to sprint out of a shed with no equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to roll along with the engine disengaged, running without being in gear.

clue.text: Where US truckers are dismissing Republican as unwilling?

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter for Republican is sent out of the longer word

parts.note: American lorry drivers travel on the interstate highways

explanation.surface: A question about where American lorry drivers end up after dropping a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Unwilling is read as un-will-ing: having made no will, and the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate has left no valid will, so they are punningly without a will.

clue.text: Seller of tickets, all for Versailles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... resells tickets at inflated prices
second meaning: the French word for all, Versailles standing for France

explanation.walkthrough: Versailles is the French palace, so it hints at a French word; the English and French words share a spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket tout is a scalper, and in French the adjective meaning every or whole is spelt the same.

clue.text: Active vent confused with flue?

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of vent and flue are jumbled together

parts.note: taken as written, as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the other half of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A heating engineer finds a working vent has been mistaken for a chimney flue.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventful period is full of incident, a busy or lively one.

clue.text: More eminent part of Oxford perhaps

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the top part of a shoe, an Oxford being a type of laced shoe

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford suggests the university, but here it is a style of lace-up shoe, whose top section has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in status, and also names the leather covering the top of a shoe.

clue.text: What sounds like quiet opportunity to eat slowly?

indicators.note: these words tell us to use a word spoken the same as the word for quiet

parts.note: peace is quiet, calm
a meal is an occasion for eating

explanation.surface: Asks what resembles a calm chance to take your time over a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done gradually, bit by bit, rather than all at once.

clue.text: Army commission rejecting place for temporary occupation

indicators.note: rejecting means the word for place is thrown out of the rank's name

parts.note: a lieutenancy is the commissioned rank of lieutenant
lieu means place, as in the phrase in lieu of

explanation.surface: An officer turns down a posting meant to be a stopgap job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenancy is the holding of property under a lease for a fixed period, so a limited possession.

clue.text: Each tune's rewritten for female singer

indicators.note: rewritten tells us the letters of these words are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Every song has been rearranged to suit a woman vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanteuse is the French loanword for a woman who sings, especially in nightclubs or cabaret.

clue.text: Heathen with yen at heart for good hymn of praise

indicators.note: for signals that one letter is put in place of another in the word for heathen

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, a non-believer

indicators.note: at heart asks for the middle letter of the word yen

parts.note: the word yen supplies its middle letter

explanation.surface: A non-believer with a longing for virtue sings a hymn of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A paean is a song of triumph or thanksgiving, originally addressed to Apollo.

clue.text: Most recent Latin is for Romans

parts.note: Lat. is the standard dictionary abbreviation for Latin
est is the Latin word for is

explanation.surface: A news item announcing that Latin is the latest Roman thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest thing is the newest, the one that has come along most recently.

clue.text: Fish bones split with time

indicators.note: split with means the word for bones is broken open to take the letter for time inside

parts.note: Bones, short for sawbones, is slang for a surgeon or doctor

explanation.surface: Describes a fish whose skeleton has broken apart over time.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for its roe, which is eaten as caviar.

clue.text: Afterburning is run and I didn't hear that swallow

parts.note: eh is the exclamation asking someone to repeat themselves
to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: Someone half-deaf mishears a remark about afterburners and jet fuel being guzzled.
explanation.definitionFit: In aviation, reheat is the British term for an afterburner system that injects fuel into a jet's exhaust.

clue.text: Gin drunk following school? Very disturbing

indicators.note: following means the jumbled gin comes after the school's name

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English boarding school in north-west London

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of gin have been knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Pupils drinking gin after school make for a shocking scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrowing experience is deeply distressing, one that torments or upsets.

clue.text: Dodgy treatment of acknowledgment in question

indicators.note: in means the acknowledgment sits inside the word for question

parts.note: a query is a question
ACK is the signal used to acknowledge receipt, as in radio and computing

explanation.surface: Questions are being raised over how an acknowledgment was handled.
explanation.definitionFit: Quackery is the practice of a charlatan offering bogus medical cures.

clue.text: Fail to win point after constant accuracy

indicators.note: after places the losing and the point behind the letter for constant

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win
a ness is a headland or point of land

explanation.surface: A sports report on a player missing a point despite steady precision.
explanation.definitionFit: Closeness can mean exactness or fidelity, as in the closeness of a translation.

clue.text: Rude joke at end of a number of addresses

indicators.note: at end of places the joke after the addresses

parts.note: homes are addresses where people live
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A vulgar quip told after a list of street addresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude in the sense of rough and unrefined matches homespun, meaning plain and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Person providing inspector with parking for Sierra

indicators.note: with parking for Sierra means the letter for parking replaces the letter for Sierra

parts.note: a surveyor inspects buildings or land
Sierra is the NATO alphabet code word for S

explanation.surface: An inspector arrives with a parking permit meant for a Ford Sierra.
explanation.definitionFit: A purveyor is a supplier, someone who provides goods such as food as a trade.

clue.text: Swineherds last seen in Hurst Green?

parts.note: pigmen are men who tend pigs

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word Hurst

parts.note: the word Hurst supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether pig farmers were last spotted at a village green called Hurst Green.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurst Green looks like an English place name; Green is the definition, an example of a colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is one example of a colouring matter or hue, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Lots of foolish people taking note

indicators.note: taking here means taking away, so the letter for note is removed

parts.note: noodle is informal for a fool, so noodles are silly people

explanation.surface: Plenty of silly people are writing down notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, plenty of something.

clue.text: Tie up south of waves breaking in gorge

indicators.note: in a down answer, south of puts the reversed tie below the waves

parts.note: surf is the foam of waves breaking on the shore

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word tie is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, the word to read backwards

explanation.surface: A surfer ties up their board beneath crashing waves in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorge looks like a ravine, but it is the verb: to eat to excess.
explanation.definitionFit: To surfeit is to overindulge or feed to excess, just as to gorge is to stuff oneself.

clue.text: Dug out Chambers — Roget's to get thrown out

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Chambers dictionary is excavated so that Roget's Thesaurus can be discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers and Roget's look like the dictionary and thesaurus on a setter's shelf; here chambers are just rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Grottoes are caves or cavern-like rooms, often hollowed out of rock.

clue.text: Agree to meet judge over statement on vacation

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the judging word above the rest

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

indicators.note: on vacation means the word statement is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the word statement supplies just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Agreeing to see a judge about a statement made while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Tryst is both a noun and a verb; as a verb it means arranging a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret rendezvous, so to tryst is to arrange a private appointment.

clue.text: Change opinion about limits on replacing one leading bishop

indicators.note: about means the change of opinion goes round the other letters

parts.note: to veer is to shift one's views or direction

indicators.note: limits on asks for the first and last letters of replacing

parts.note: the word replacing supplies its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A churchman reconsiders the rules on substituting a senior bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A verger is a church official who walks ahead of clergy in processions, carrying a staff.

clue.text: Thin cloth, uniform in look

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for uniform goes inside the word for look

parts.note: to gaze is to look steadily
Uniform is the NATO alphabet code word for U

explanation.surface: A uniform made of flimsy material catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauze is a light, transparent woven fabric used for bandages and veils.

clue.text: Satellite low on nitrogen

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the lowing above the nitrogen

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: A space probe running short of nitrogen.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon is Earth's natural satellite, the body orbiting our planet.

clue.text: Improve morally and turn to God with advancing ecstasy

indicators.note: advancing means the drug letter moves forward to the front
with signals the word is taken together with its drug letter moved

parts.note: to deify is to make into a god

explanation.surface: A suggestion that taking ecstasy might bring about religious conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for the drug ecstasy; it moves one place forward in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone so as to improve them morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Try plain language and shorten English

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language as opposed to verse
to cut is to shorten

explanation.surface: Advice to write in simple words and trim your English.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosecute someone is to bring them to trial, so try in its legal sense.

clue.text: Bet on lengthiest struggling and economise

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters writhe about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, these are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gambler backs the longest-odds horse and has to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten one's belt is an idiom for spending less and living more frugally.
